storylines.title: Olympiacos Pursuing John Konchar
storylines.summary: EuroLeague power Olympiacos is pursuing veteran NBA wing John Konchar. Olympiacos is looking for reinforcements on the perimeter after some recent turbulence with their roster. Konchar was signed to a training camp deal with the New York Knicks. The 6-foot-5 guard/forward was considered a favorite to land an opening night spot, but was waive near the start of camp to attend to a personal issue. Olympiacos lost wing Shaquielle McKissic in the offseason. Then veteran wing Evan Fournier suffered a sprained MCL in his right knee and a bruised shoulder. On top of those absences, guard Tyler Dorsey was suspended by the Greek club after complaining publicly about his role and contract. There had been speculation that Konchar could land with another NBA team later in the season. Several teams are carrying open roster spots, but a handful won't be able to fill them until they're deeper into the season due to lack of room under a incurred hard cap.

storylines.title: NBA Generated $14.5 Billion In Revenue Last Season, Led By Warriors' $895M
storylines.summary: The NBA generated approximately $14.5 billion in revenue during the 2025-26 season. The 30 teams brought in a combined $13.7 billion, an average of $456 million each, with the rest kept at the league level. The Golden State Warriors led all teams with $895 million in revenue. The Memphis Grizzlies ranked last at $339 million. The totals are after revenue sharing, which moved about $400 million to lower-revenue teams. The NBA's 11-year, $76 billion media deal raised each team's national TV payout from $103 million to $144 million last season. Those payments will rise by approximately seven percent a year on average. Central league revenue made up 41 percent of team revenue. Seating and luxury suites brought in an estimated $3.64 billion. The Warriors led the league with nearly $5.5 million in ticket revenue per game, and the Los Angeles Lakers and New York Knicks each topped $4 million. The Knicks' playoff run generated $180 million in gross revenue. Sponsorships totaled $1.9 billion. Golden State's sponsorship revenue was about $190 million and should top $200 million this season with a new jersey patch deal worth more than $50 million a year. Local media revenue is expected to drop this season after Main Street Sports' bankruptcy affected 13 teams. The Lakers have the NBA's biggest local TV deal, worth about $200 million a year with Spectrum. The average NBA franchise is now worth $6.64 billion, up 21 percent from last year. If Las Vegas and Seattle both join the league, each existing owner would receive more than $500 million in expansion fees, which are not shared with players. The league has said it will decide on expansion by the end of the calendar year.
